title: Sign Acts of the Prophets
lead: Messages that a prophet acted out instead of, or as well as, speaking: Ahijah tearing a robe (1 Kings 11:29-31), Isaiah going barefoot and stripped for three years (Isaiah 20:2-4), Jeremiah's linen belt, broken jar and yoke (Jeremiah 13:1-11; 19:1-13; 27:1-2), Hosea's marriage (Hosea 1:2-9; 3:1-5), Ezekiel's brick, long lying on his side, rationed bread and shaved hair (Ezekiel 4-5), his packed bags (Ezekiel 12:1-16), his silent grief at his wife's death (Ezekiel 24:15-27) and the two sticks joined in his hand (Ezekiel 37:15-23), and Agabus's binding of his own feet and hands in the New Testament (Acts 21:10-11). Scholars debate whether each act was done in public or told as a vision.
